overview: Olmec names a group of early Mesoamerican societies, especially those of Mexico's Gulf Coast. Their monumental building projects and stoneworking joined local farming communities to far-reaching networks of materials and artistic ideas.

items.text: At San Lorenzo, communities cooperated to build large earthen platforms and mounds. These were shared construction projects beyond the needs of individual households.
Artists worked both enormous volcanic-stone sculptures and small, finely finished jade objects. Those materials could travel from distant sources.
Maize farming helped sustain communities in Gulf Coast river valleys, although many details of San Lorenzo's households remain under investigation.
Rubber balls recovered at El Manati provide early evidence for the place of ballgames in Olmec life.
La Venta's carvings connect rulers with watery environments and agricultural fertility. Their imagery draws on the surrounding landscape.
La Venta flourished especially between 1000 and 500 BCE and was apparently abandoned by 400 BCE. That local sequence does not establish one universal fall for all Olmec societies.
